nodes.long_description:
It's 1991. Your brother is gone. What he left is his room, a beige PC, a dial-up modem, a stack of floppies and a rent bill with a deadline.

THE PC IS REAL
Boot it, install games from floppies, buy a faster CPU, video card and hard disk and switch them on in the BIOS. Everything runs on a simulated machine, and every program can be opened and changed.

WORK THE LINE
Dial in, read your mail and take jobs: fix broken programs, decode secret messages, test games. Get paid (eventually), build trust and chase the clients who don't pay.

GO DEEPER
Follow the white rabbit into a hidden network. Scan hosts, sniff traffic and crack passwords in puzzles that reward skill, not luck. Somewhere at the end of the trail is the reason your brother disappeared.

MAKE YOUR OWN
Learn the built-in language step by step, then make 2D, tile-map or 3D games, pack them onto floppies and publish them. After the story, free play keeps the whole machine yours.

AN OLD INTERNET
Text-mode web pages, slow-loading GIFs, chat rooms full of theories, shady download sites and viruses waiting for the careless.

PLAY YOUR WAY
Sit at the desk in VR, or play on your monitor with mouse and keyboard. A keyboard is recommended for coding.
nodes.short_description: Your older brother vanished and left you his room, his early-90s PC and a dial-up modem. Take coding jobs to pay the rent, fix bugs, crack codes and slip into a hidden network while you follow his trail. Then write your own games in the built-in language, pack them on floppies and share them. Sit at the desk in VR or play on your monitor.

nodes.change_log:
# 1.4.8 f2  23.11.2026
- Selling a spare RAM stick takes the loose one, never the
one in the running PC
- Byte Bazaar no longer offers the board in your PC for sale
- Saves from before the hand-built PC no longer push 1 MB
sticks into a board that can't take them; a PC left with no
memory it takes gets a stick that fits
- The TX586 board shows its texture
- Pindows: running a game from a floppy no longer breaks the
PC, and VOS Commander opened from Pindows runs floppies and
notices when one is taken out
- Deleted downloads (TurboTune setup, Lunix disk images) no
longer come back after a restart
- Boot console: cd \lunix\root and other paths from C:\
work, Tab completes inside folders, ls takes a folder, and
\t or \r no longer turn into a tab or a new line
* 3D Chess 1.2.3: beating the computer unlocks its
achievement, games end in a draw on threefold repetition or
50 moves without a capture, GLOW and GRAIN show more, and
it stays smoother while the computer thinks. Reinstall it
from the disks or C:\DOWNLOADS to update

# 1.4.8 f1  22.11.2026
+ Motherboards: four boards to collect and swap by hand -
VRK AT286, VL486, TX586 and BX370. Each takes its own CPUs
and memory, and its slots take only the cards of their bus
(ISA, VLB, PCI, AGP). Find them in the shop under Boards
+ Old saves carry over: you get the board your CPU needs, and
any part a board can't take goes back on the shelf, boxed
+ CrossFlyer: the BX370 has two AGP slots. Fit a second ADI
Padeon 64 Pro and the cards link up for faster 3D
* 3D video cards now work beside the CPU instead of eating its
time: a frame takes as long as the slower of the two, so a
better card (or two) really lifts heavy 3D
* GPUMARK has six new scenes: rock-and-moss terrain from
marching cubes, a Matrix flyby, 3D metaballs, a ray tracer
with mirror and glass balls, 3D chess (CPU plays, GPU draws)
and the night city. It measures without the 60 Hz limit, so
every card and CrossFlyer shows in the score. Pindows has its
icon in Main
+ Three new achievements: beat TEXEL_TERMINATOR in GPUMARK,
link two cards with the CrossFlyer bridge, and a secret one
+ Earn stickers for the tower's front: Pindows, Lunix,
MEGAMARK #1 and CrossFlyer
* Memory sticks fit the board's era: 1 and 2 MB sticks are
30-pin (AT286, VL486), 4 MB and up 72-pin (all but AT286)
+ Real BIOS beep codes: the PC speaker tells you what is
wrong when the PC won't start
+ POST card: an ISA diagnostic card whose display shows the
code where the start-up stopped
* New IDE and floppy ribbon cables and separate power wires
in the case; the drive cage and the 286 chip look the part
* ADI Padeon 64 Pro redesigned, with its red lines lit while
the PC runs; the NOPUA cooler sits further forward, so the
memory slots are easier to reach
* V-Force 2MX, 3 and 4 now each look like their own card, and
the sound card is redone; boxes and shop pictures to match
+ The VRK AT286 is true to its time: 30-pin memory (the 1 and
2 MB sticks), and a drive controller card in ISA4 that the
IDE and floppy ribbons plug into
* Drive power uses real Molex plugs, and the power leads leave
the PSU through a braided sleeve
+ The BX370 takes ATX power: one 20-pin plug instead of P8/P9,
and a standby light on the board while the PSU has power
* The TX586 has an ATX header beside its AT one, as many 1997
boards did
* A board held up close fills more of the view
+ Lunix: rm, mv, cp, mkdir, touch, ps and kill
- Lunix vee: Enter and Backspace no longer act twice
- Holding an arrow key repeats it in Lunix and Notepad
- My downloads: cancel a download; UNDERNET files say when
they wait for the UNDERNET line
- PC sound comes from the speakers by the monitor, in stereo,
not from near the printer and the left ear only
- VHS: the picture no longer shows past the TV's edges, and
wide videos are no longer cropped
- MAPEDIT.INI errors show the line that was not understood,
and a ; note after a [things] or [tags] line is allowed
- A screen left over from start-up could cover the monitor
and leave programs on a blue screen
- Typing ^ and other dead keys works on Nordic keyboards
- Pindows Notepad: Page Up / Page Down move a window at a time
- JOBS: a long brief scrolls with Page Up / Page Down or the
wheel instead of running under the goals
- Pindows Notepad: Shift selects, Ctrl+C / X / V use the
clipboard, and typing replaces the selection
- Pindows: file names starting with t or n show correctly
- DOS dialogs: a stray < no longer shifts the buttons
+ VOS Commander: Copy (F5) and Move (F6) ask where to, with
the other panel's folder filled in
+ BYTE BAZAAR: donate your old starter parts to Ram
Altman's ChadGPT (http://chadgpt)
+ Give away all your basic parts and ChadGPT itself wants
to chat - donate a cooler to stop its crashes
* Deliveries ring the doorbell, and parcels thud as they land
- A written-off invoice shows as CLOSED in JOBS, My jobs
- W/S no longer jumps two lines at a time in menus
- Text windows over Pindows no longer let lines show
through
- The shop no longer offers RAM sticks of a size you
already have four of

# 1.4.7f3  21.11.2026
+ Programs can use the mouse: GetMouseX, GetMouseY, GetMouseButton,
GetMouseButtonDown and GetMouseWheel (a finger on the screen in VR).
See the guide's INPUT chapter and the new C:\EXAMPLES\MOUSE. PONG's
paddle follows the mouse too
+ EDIT: Ctrl+Backspace / Ctrl+Delete erase a whole word, and
Ctrl+Left / Right jump by word (add Shift to select)
* The pointer speed set in Pindows' Control Panel now also
applies outside Pindows: VRKNavigator, PAINT, COMPOSER...
- Pindows: a maximised window fills only the part the monitor
shows, so its title bar buttons stay in reach (and double-click
on a title bar restores it, as in 3.1)
- Pindows: double-clicking a group icon or a title bar no longer
also opens the program that ends up under the pointer
- Notepad: a line longer than the window scrolls sideways with
the cursor instead of being cut off with "..."
+ Notepad: Ctrl+A selects everything, Ctrl+Backspace / Delete
erase a word, Ctrl+Left / Right jump by word
- Boot console help lists only V-OS commands, lined up, and
PgUp / PgDn scroll the console
- Boot console: clear works again, and natives prints the whole
list instead of an error
- MAIL: long replies no longer push the Back button off the
screen
- PONG: the paddles were hidden at the screen edges at 800x600;
the game now scales to the screen and keeps inside it, and a
fast ball no longer slips through a paddle

# 1.4.5f  18.11.2026
+ Build your PC by hand: a new tower with the side panel off.
Walk up and work inside the case to take parts out, swap them
and fit new ones - CPU, cooler, video and sound cards, memory
and hard disk. What is in the case is what your PC has
+ Parts you order now come in their retail boxes: the doorbell
rings and the courier drops them by the door. Open a box and
fit the part yourself
+ The BIOS checks the case at power-on and tells you what is
missing - no CPU fan, no memory, no boot disk
+ Fans spin and the LEDs light up while the PC runs
+ No sound card in the case, no sound: games, music and the
sound tools tell you it is missing and the PC stays silent
+ MEGAMARK 2000 (http://megamark): benchmark your PC, submit
your score to the Hall of Speed and beat the overclockers
+ Kev's H2O-MAX 2000 water cooling, plain or RGB EDITION, sold
by Kev himself in the MEGAMARK classifieds. Cooler CPU, more
TurboTune headroom. Mind the hose clamps
+ Two new air coolers in the VRK shop: the ZALKAN Bloom 7 copper
flower and the NOPUA DT-2 twin tower. Cooler than the stock fan
and more overclocking room, without Kev's hose clamps
+ Beat KEV_H2O and the EXTREME section opens: dry ice
+ 3 new achievements: water cooling, going RGB, and a new
MEGAMARK world record
+ Spare parts live on the bookshelves, each in its own place.
Leave a part anywhere you like - next time you play it is back
in its box on the shelf. Free play starts with every part, Kev's
kits and the dry ice already there
+ Overclock from the BIOS: Setup has a FREQUENCY/VOLTAGE CONTROL
page - CPU and video clocks and CPU core voltage. More volts keep
a high clock stable but run hotter. Works in DOS, Pindows and Lunix
* TurboTune: how far you can push now depends on your cooling
* Your old PC moves into the new case by itself: the parts you
had installed are fitted, the spare parts you own wait boxed
on the bookshelves. Credits, files and progress stay as they were
* The shop sells up to four memory sticks of each size - that
fills every bank
* DOOM WADs and files you copy in from outside no longer count
against your hard disk
* A disk too small for drive C: no longer stops the PC - it
boots and warns you the disk is full
* Start Over also uninstalls Pindows, TurboTune and Lunix and
resets LOLO to DOS: a new career earns them again

# 1.3.8  13.11.2026
- Balloons vs Ghosts 1.1 would not start after installing it:
a file was missing from the package. 1.1.1 is on GamezPot -
download it again and install it over the old one, your
scores stay
- DZMARIO 2.0.7: a khinkali popping out of a block makes its
sound again. Download it again from GamezPot to update
* Games in C:\DOWNLOADS that GamezPot has updated since you
downloaded them refresh themselves - just install them again
- Pindows File Manager and Lunix xfm now open what VOS
Commander opens: .VPK packages install with SETUP, and level
packs, modem firmware and WADs work from there too
- Lunix can no longer be started from inside DOS or Pindows -
pick it in LOLO at power-on
+ Pindows and Lunix: pictures open in a viewer, sounds and
songs in a small player, with Edit for PAINT, SNDEDIT or
COMPOSER when you have them

# 1.3.7  11.11.2026
+ LOLO boot loader: pick DOS, Pindows or Lunix at power-on.
Change the default, the wait and the names in LOLO's options,
with BOOTCFG at the DOS prompt or Boot Manager in Pindows
+ Lunix 0.99 (Slackwire): a free Unix-like system on two floppies,
from the slackwire FTP on UNDERNET. Write them with RAWRITE,
boot the first one and follow the installer.
DOS and Pindows stay where they are
+ Lunix boots to a root shell - ls, cd, cat, df, free, uname...
and runs the V-OS programs under dosemu (try: dosemu mail)
+ vee, Lunix's own text editor. If you know vi, you know vee.
If you don't: i to type, Esc, then :wq to save and quit
+ startx (4 MB RAM): an X desktop with fvwm, four desks and
a pager, a panel with clock, load, credits, modem and mail,
and xterm, xfm, xedit, xclock and xload. X remembers your
windows for the next session
+ Pindows: drag a window's edge or corner to resize it.
Program windows open where you left them
+ Balloons vs Ghosts 1.1 on GamezPot. Own it already? GamezPot
shows the update - download it again and install it over the
old one in VOS Commander, your scores stay
+ 5 new achievements, two of them hidden
* Mouse pointers are smaller
- Floppies you write now show their label, and the right name
when you pick them up

MACROHARD PINDOWS 3.12
- A windowed OS for your 1991 PC, bought in the VRK Shop and delivered as a boxed set of six floppies
- Wait for the parcel by the door, pin the CD key on the cork board, feed SETUP disks 1 to 6
- File Manager, Notepad, System Info with a VRK-GL test, and the MacroHard Navigator web browser
- Two games: Minefield and Patience (yes, the bouncing cards)
- Desktop shortcuts, wallpapers and colours in Control Panel
- Swap a CPU or video card and Pindows runs Add New Hardware and installs a driver

TURBOTUNE 95
- On VRK-NET: overclock the CPU and video card, set the fan, watch the temperature
- Burn-in with the Donut Test: FPS and MAX FPS
- Push it too far and meet the pink screen of death

BALLOONS VS GHOSTS
- New on GamezPot: tie balloons to the lawn and keep the ghosts out of the house. 10 levels, a top 10, 75 CR

LANGUAGES
- Italiano: pick it on first launch or in Settings
- Phone calls have Georgian voices when the game is in Georgian
- Pindows, its programs and TurboTune speak every language the game does

ALSO
- A new TODO task, and new chat in #hardware and #games
